title: Schedule: View grants the full read experience - page, all three views, mini calendar, search, filter, tooltips, read-only modals
permissions_required: A role with Schedule: View but NOT Schedule: Edit (for example Technician, Parts Manager, Parts Tech, Office, or Time Clock). Set up the test user's role at VIU per Standing Rule 5 and restore after.
preconditions: 1. A test user's role has Schedule: View but NOT Edit (assign a suitable system role or a purpose-made custom role; restore after).
2. Shifts and events exist on the grid, created by an Edit-capable user.
3. You are signed in AS that View-only user on a desktop browser.
steps: 1. Open the Schedule page.
2. Switch between Day, Week, and Month.
3. Use the mini calendar, the toolbar search, and the sidebar filter.
4. Hover a shift for its tooltip, then click it to open the detail modal.
expected: 1. The Schedule page opens and all three views work.
2. The mini calendar, search, and filters all work.
3. ALL technicians' shifts and events are visible (not just the user's own).
4. Tooltips show on hover, and the shift/event detail modals open in read-only mode.
design_ref: Claude design (authoritative, Branko Q0): build/schedule/spec-v1-2026-07-22/design-notes-claude.md (prototype Schedule.dc.html). spec_1 added the Design link to the doc.
notes: Ask the user at VIU how the Schedule permission tier appears in the roles admin (exact permission names). Verify per role LIVE (Standing Rules 10/12/13) - never derive from role definitions.

title: View-only: every editing affordance is hidden or disabled
permissions_required: A role with Schedule: View but NOT Edit.
preconditions: 1. A test user's role has Schedule: View but NOT Edit.
2. Shifts, a series, and events exist on the grid.
3. You are signed in AS that View-only user on a desktop browser, on the Schedule page.
steps: 1. Look for drag handles on sidebar lines and try to drag a work order card onto the grid.
2. Try dragging an existing shift block (move/reassign) and look for resize handles in day view.
3. Right-click a grid cell.
4. Open a shift's detail modal and inspect its fields and actions.
expected: 1. No drag handles are offered and nothing can be dragged from the sidebar onto the grid.
2. Shift blocks cannot be moved or resized - no drop targets or resize handles appear.
3. The right-click context menu does not appear (no New Shift / New Event / View Day creation entry points).
4. In the modal, edit fields are hidden or disabled, and the reassign and delete actions are absent.
design_ref: Claude design (authoritative, Branko Q0): build/schedule/spec-v1-2026-07-22/design-notes-claude.md (prototype Schedule.dc.html). spec_1 added the Design link to the doc.
spec_ref: requirements.md §14.1 (Schedule: View - editing affordances hidden or disabled)
refs: SV-8685 (§14.1 (Schedule: View - editing affordances hidden or disabled))
notes: Spec allows 'hidden or disabled' - record which of the two the build does for each affordance.

title: With Schedule: View OFF, the Schedule top-level nav item is hidden entirely
permissions_required: A role with NO Schedule permissions at all.
preconditions: 1. A test user's role has Schedule: View OFF (no Schedule permission).
2. You are signed in AS that user on a desktop browser.
steps: 1. Look at the app's main navigation.
2. Search the nav for any Schedule entry.
expected: 1. The Schedule top-level nav item is not shown at all.
2. The rest of the app works normally for the role.
design_ref: Claude design (authoritative, Branko Q0): build/schedule/spec-v1-2026-07-22/design-notes-claude.md (prototype Schedule.dc.html). spec_1 added the Design link to the doc.
notes: The spec pins only the nav being hidden. Also probe direct URL access at VIU and record the observed behavior (not spec-pinned - do not assert a specific redirect).

title: Schedule: Edit unlocks all creation and modification interactions
permissions_required: A role with Schedule: Edit (requires View) - per spec the level for Service Manager, Senior Service Advisor, Service Advisor, and Foreman.
preconditions: 1. A test user's role has Schedule: Edit (and View) but NOT Delete.
2. Work orders with approved lines exist; you are signed in AS that user, on the Schedule page.
steps: 1. Drag a work order from the sidebar onto a technician cell and complete the scope picker (and spread modal for a large job).
2. Right-click a cell and create an event via 'New Event'; in day view, click empty space to create.
3. Reassign a shift between technicians by dragging.
4. In day view, edge-resize and horizontally drag a shift.
5. Edit fields in the shift and event detail modals.
expected: 1. Drag-and-drop from the sidebar, the scope picker, and the spread modal all work.
2. Shift and event creation works, including via the right-click context menu and day-view click-to-create.
3. Reassignment between technicians works.
4. Edge-resize and horizontal drag work in day view.
5. Modal fields are editable and save.
design_ref: Claude design (authoritative, Branko Q0): build/schedule/spec-v1-2026-07-22/design-notes-claude.md (prototype Schedule.dc.html). spec_1 added the Design link to the doc.

title: Edit without Delete: the user can create and modify but cannot remove - delete action and trash icon hidden
permissions_required: A role with Schedule: Edit but NOT Schedule: Delete.
preconditions: 1. A test user's role has Schedule: Edit but NOT Delete.
2. A shift, a series, and an event exist (some created by this user).
3. You are signed in AS that user, on the Schedule page.
steps: 1. Open a shift's detail modal and look for the delete action / trash icon.
2. Open an event's modal and look for a delete action.
3. Try to find ANY way to remove a shift or event.
expected: 1. The delete action and the trash icon are hidden in the shift modal.
2. Events likewise offer no delete.
3. No path exists to remove shifts or events - while creating and modifying still work (per SCH-PERM-04).
design_ref: Claude design (authoritative, Branko Q0): build/schedule/spec-v1-2026-07-22/design-notes-claude.md (prototype Schedule.dc.html). spec_1 added the Design link to the doc.

title: Schedule: Delete unlocks deleting shifts and events, including the three series-aware scopes
permissions_required: A role with Schedule: Delete (requires Edit, which requires View).
preconditions: 1. A test user's role has Schedule: Delete.
2. A standalone shift, a series, and an event exist.
3. You are signed in AS that user, on the Schedule page.
steps: 1. Delete the standalone shift.
2. Delete a series shift and read the scope options.
3. Delete the event.
expected: 1. The delete action is available and works for shifts.
2. Series deletion offers its scopes (this shift / this and after / whole series).
3. Events can be deleted too.
4. Undo toasts appear (restore the items via Undo to clean up).
design_ref: Claude design (authoritative, Branko Q0): build/schedule/spec-v1-2026-07-22/design-notes-claude.md (prototype Schedule.dc.html). spec_1 added the Design link to the doc.

title: The permission tiers depend on each other: Delete requires Edit, and Edit requires View
permissions_required: Admin access to the roles screen (to inspect/set the Schedule permission tiers on a custom role).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in as an admin who can edit custom roles.
2. A ZZAUTOTEST custom role exists (create one; delete after).
steps: 1. In the role's Schedule permissions, try to enable Edit while View is off.
2. Try to enable Delete while Edit is off.
3. Enable View, then Edit, then Delete in order.
expected: 1. Edit cannot be granted without View (the admin UI enforces or auto-selects the dependency).
2. Delete cannot be granted without Edit.
3. The three tiers can be enabled in dependency order, so each higher level always includes the ones beneath it (Delete includes Edit, and Edit includes View).
design_ref: Claude design (authoritative, Branko Q0): build/schedule/spec-v1-2026-07-22/design-notes-claude.md (prototype Schedule.dc.html). spec_1 added the Design link to the doc.
spec_ref: requirements.md §14 (Delete requires Edit and Edit requires View)
refs: SV-8685 (§14 (Delete requires Edit and Edit requires View))
notes: How the roles admin enforces the dependency (disabled checkbox vs auto-check) is not pinned - record the observed mechanism live.

title: Schedule access without Work Orders: View - sidebar hides the WO list and drill-down; mini calendar stays; grid shifts remain usable
permissions_required: A role with Schedule: View (or higher) but Work Orders: View OFF.
preconditions: 1. A test user's role has Schedule access but Work Orders: View OFF.
2. Shifts already exist on the grid.
3. You are signed in AS that user, on the Schedule page.
steps: 1. Look at the left sidebar.
2. Interact with the shifts already on the grid (hover, open modal, and - if the role has Edit - move one).
3. Try to find any way to drag a new work order onto the grid.
expected: 1. The sidebar hides the work order list and the line drill-down; the mini calendar remains available.
2. Shifts already on the grid can still be viewed and interacted with per the role's Schedule tier.
3. New work orders cannot be dragged on - the WO list is simply not visible.
design_ref: Claude design (authoritative, Branko Q0): build/schedule/spec-v1-2026-07-22/design-notes-claude.md (prototype Schedule.dc.html). spec_1 added the Design link to the doc.

title: No own-only restriction: every Schedule: View user sees ALL technicians' shifts and events
permissions_required: A low-tier role with Schedule: View (for example Technician or Time Clock).
preconditions: 1. Shifts and events exist for SEVERAL different technicians.
2. A test user with a low-tier View-only role exists (and is themselves one of the technicians).
3. You are signed in AS that user, on the Schedule page.
steps: 1. Read the grid across all departments and technicians.
2. Check 'My Shifts' in 'Filter and Display' is OFF (default).
expected: 1. The user sees ALL technicians' shifts and events, not only their own - there is no role-based 'own shifts only' restriction.
2. 'My Shifts' exists only as an optional personal convenience filter (off by default), not a security boundary.
design_ref: Claude design (authoritative, Branko Q0): build/schedule/spec-v1-2026-07-22/design-notes-claude.md (prototype Schedule.dc.html). spec_1 added the Design link to the doc.

title: Grid rows are department-based: any staff member in a visible department appears as a row, regardless of role
permissions_required: Admin access to staff records for setup; any Schedule: View user to observe.
preconditions: 1. A staff member with a NON-technician role (for example Office) is assigned to a department that is visible on the schedule (set up; restore after).
2. Another staff member has NO department assignment.
3. You are signed in on a desktop browser, on the Schedule page.
steps: 1. Look for the department-assigned Office staff member among the grid rows.
2. Look for the staff member with no department.
expected: 1. The department-assigned staff member appears as a technician row - row presence is controlled by the department on the staff record, NOT by role permission.
2. The staff member without a department does not appear as a row.
design_ref: Claude design (authoritative, Branko Q0): build/schedule/spec-v1-2026-07-22/design-notes-claude.md (prototype Schedule.dc.html). spec_1 added the Design link to the doc.
notes: Expectation 2 is the contrapositive derivation of §14.4 - confirm live how department-less staff are handled.

title: Clocking into work order line tasks is gated by the staff record's 'Time Clock' setting, not the permission model
permissions_required: Admin access to staff records for setup; the affected staff user to observe.
preconditions: 1. Two staff members exist: one with the 'Time Clock' setting ON on their staff record, one with it OFF (set up; restore after).
2. Both appear as schedule rows and have shifts on work order lines.
steps: 1. As (or with) the Time-Clock-ON staff member, attempt to clock into their work order line task.
2. As (or with) the Time-Clock-OFF staff member, attempt the same.
expected: 1. The Time-Clock-ON staff member can clock in.
2. The Time-Clock-OFF staff member cannot - the ability is controlled by the staff-record setting, not by the Schedule permission tier.
design_ref: Claude design (authoritative, Branko Q0): build/schedule/spec-v1-2026-07-22/design-notes-claude.md (prototype Schedule.dc.html). spec_1 added the Design link to the doc.
notes: The clock-in surface (where clock-in happens relative to the schedule) is not described in this spec - locate it live.

title: With Work Orders: View OFF, work-order-derived details on shifts (customer, lines, money fields) are hidden or masked
permissions_required: A role with Schedule: View (or higher) but Work Orders: View OFF. Set up the test user's role at VIU per Standing Rule 5 and restore after.
preconditions: 1. A test user's role has Schedule access but Work Orders: View OFF (assign a suitable role; restore after).
2. Shifts already exist on the grid, created by a fully-permissioned user, for units that have customers, scheduled lines, and a VIN.
3. You are signed in AS that user on a desktop browser, on the Schedule page.
steps: 1. Look at a shift block on the grid and read its text lines.
2. Hover the shift for its tooltip.
3. Open the shift's detail modal and read the work-order-derived fields.
expected: 1. Work-order-derived details (customer, the scheduled line list, and any money-bearing fields) are hidden or masked wherever they would normally appear - on the block, in the tooltip, and in the modal.
2. The schedule structure itself (the shift's day, time, and technician) stays visible so the grid remains usable.
3. This extends the sidebar behavior (the work order list and drill-down are hidden) to the work-order data surfaced on the shifts themselves.
design_ref: Claude design (authoritative, Branko Q0): build/schedule/spec-v1-2026-07-22/design-notes-claude.md (prototype Schedule.dc.html). spec_1 added the Design link to the doc.
notes: NEW case (reconciliation 2026-07-22). Driver: Branko Q&A 2026-07-22 Q3 ('We do not show total $ anywhere in the schedule. We can hide other items that fall under that permission'). Complements the sidebar-hide permission case. Confirm the exact masking (hidden vs placeholder) live at VIU. No TestRail C-id yet - pending authorized add_case.

title: Planned hours across technicians may exceed the estimate - accepted without error
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A work order line with a 40h estimate exists.
steps: 1. Spread the full estimate onto technician A.
2. Spread the full estimate of the SAME work order onto technician B.
3. Look for any warning or error about exceeding the estimate.
expected: 1. Both series are created - 80 planned hours against a 40h estimate is accepted.

2. No error or blocking warning appears - this is expected behavior because progress is driven by clocked-in time, and scheduled hours, the estimate, and actual hours are three separate quantities that are not forced to reconcile.
design_ref: Claude design (authoritative, Branko Q0): build/schedule/spec-v1-2026-07-22/design-notes-claude.md (prototype Schedule.dc.html). spec_1 added the Design link to the doc.

title: Below 960px the grid scrolls horizontally, and the sidebar collapses on narrow viewports
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Schedule page in week view with shifts visible.
steps: 1. Resize the browser window to just under 960px wide.
2. Try to reach the right-hand days of the grid.
3. Narrow the window further and watch the sidebar.
expected: 1. Below the 960px minimum supported width, the grid scrolls horizontally rather than breaking.
2. All days remain reachable by horizontal scroll.
3. On narrow viewports the sidebar collapses.
4. No content becomes permanently unreachable and nothing errors.
design_ref: Claude design (authoritative, Branko Q0): build/schedule/spec-v1-2026-07-22/design-notes-claude.md (prototype Schedule.dc.html). spec_1 added the Design link to the doc.
notes: The exact collapse breakpoint for the sidebar is not pinned (only 'narrow viewports') - record the observed breakpoint live. 960px threshold itself - confirm live.

title: The sidebar work order list and line drill-down stay smooth with 50+ items
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. 50 or more open work orders exist (seed ZZAUTOTEST orders if the environment lacks them), including one order with many approved lines.
3. You are on the Schedule page.
steps: 1. Scroll the full work order list top to bottom quickly.
2. Open the many-line order's drill-down and scroll it.
3. Type in the search while the long list is shown.
expected: 1. Scrolling stays smooth with no long freezes or blank stretches that fail to fill in (the list virtualizes at 50+ items).
2. The drill-down behaves the same with many lines.
3. Search stays responsive on the long list.
design_ref: Claude design (authoritative, Branko Q0): build/schedule/spec-v1-2026-07-22/design-notes-claude.md (prototype Schedule.dc.html). spec_1 added the Design link to the doc.
notes: Virtualization itself is an implementation detail - the observable assertion is smoothness; treat visible jank/freeze as the failure signal.

title: The grid renders smoothly at full load - 15 technicians × 7 days with several shifts per cell
permissions_required: Schedule: View to observe; Edit to seed (spec §14.1).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. The schedule is loaded to roughly the spec's stated scale: around 15 technician rows across a week with several shifts per cell (seed ZZAUTOTEST shifts as needed).
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Scroll the grid vertically and horizontally.
2. Switch between Day, Week, and Month.
3. Hover several blocks and open/close a modal.
expected: 1. The grid renders and scrolls smoothly at this scale.
2. View switches complete without long hangs.
3. Tooltips and modals stay responsive.
design_ref: Claude design (authoritative, Branko Q0): build/schedule/spec-v1-2026-07-22/design-notes-claude.md (prototype Schedule.dc.html). spec_1 added the Design link to the doc.
notes: Perception-based smoothness check - record any measurable jank observed.

title: Shop closures do NOT block spread in V1 - shifts can land on closure days
permissions_required: Schedule: Edit + admin access to define a shop closure.
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A shop closure (holiday/inventory day) is defined at the shop level on a working weekday inside the planned spread window (set it up; remove after).
3. A large job (multi-day scope) is ready to spread.
steps: 1. Open the spread step across a window that contains a shop closure day.
2. Expand the preview and find the closure day.
3. Confirm the spread and check the grid.
expected: 1. The closure day is NOT struck through or skipped by the spread in V1.
2. A shift CAN be placed on the shop closure day (only weekend days with no business hours are skipped).
3. The end date follows the normal daily distribution - no extra day is added for the closure.
design_ref: Claude design (authoritative, Branko Q0): build/schedule/spec-v1-2026-07-22/design-notes-claude.md (prototype Schedule.dc.html). spec_1 added the Design link to the doc.
notes: V1 rule (Jira SV-8691 Key Decision, latest-wins over the older requirements.md §12): shop closures / public holidays are NOT skipped by spread in V1. This reverses the earlier 'closures block spread' expectation. Driver: SV-8691 §4.5, §12. Verify live at VIU.

title: Scheduled hours, the estimate, and actual (clocked) hours are three separate quantities that are not forced to reconcile
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A line has estimate 10h; a technician has 6h scheduled against it and some different amount of time actually clocked (seed what is possible).
steps: 1. Open the shift's detail modal.
2. Compare the scheduled hours, the estimate, and the logged/actual time.
expected: 1. All three quantities are shown/derivable and may differ from one another.
2. Nothing forces them to match - no error, no auto-correction (progress is driven by clocked-in time).
design_ref: Claude design (authoritative, Branko Q0): build/schedule/spec-v1-2026-07-22/design-notes-claude.md (prototype Schedule.dc.html). spec_1 added the Design link to the doc.
